# Intake brief — Shields need to pulse and fade when ending (AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC)

## Problem statement

The P3 Shield shows a static bubble for its full 15-second duration and then
vanishes instantly at expiry. Players get no warning that the shield is about
to drop, so the moment the shield is gone is unpredictable and reads as a bug.

## Users

- **Player (primary).** As a player, when my P3 shield is about to expire I
  want the bubble to visibly wind down (pulse + fade) over the final second so
  I know to reposition before I become vulnerable.
- **Developer / maintainer (secondary).** As a maintainer, I want the ending
  animation to live in the one shared visual helper so the game and every gym
  stay identical and cannot drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — While P3 is active with **more than 1.0 s** remaining, the bubble
  keeps its current steady-state appearance (fill alpha `0.12`, stroke alpha
  `0.9`, radius `SHIP_SIZE × 1.6`); no pulsing.
- **AC2** — During the **final 1.0 s** of P3 (remaining ≤ 1.0 s), the shared
  helper draws an "ending" indicator: the fill becomes visibly **opaque**
  (fill alpha ramps up above `SHIELD_BUBBLE_FILL_ALPHA`, e.g. to a documented
  `SHIELD_BUBBLE_ENDING_FILL_ALPHA`) and the **rim pulses** (stroke alpha
  oscillates) for the whole second.
- **AC3** — During the **final 0.5 s** (remaining ≤ 0.5 s), the fill/shading
  **shrinks monotonically** from the full bubble radius (`SHIP_SIZE × 1.6`)
  toward a radius **below the ship hull radius** (`SHIP_SIZE / 2`), so the
  shield visually reads as ineffective; at expiry the bubble is cleared and
  nothing is drawn.
- **AC4** — The animation is owned by the shared `CombatEffectVisuals` helper
  and parametrised only by `registry.remaining('P3')`, so `PlayScene`,
  `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` render it identically with no
  per-scene duplication; all thresholds/colours are exported constants.
- **AC5** — Unit tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` cover:
  steady-state above 1 s; opaque fill + pulsing rim in the final second; fill
  radius shrinking below `SHIP_SIZE / 2` in the final half second; bubble
  cleared at expiry; determinism for a given remaining time. The same tests
  assert the helper is safe with no graphics/player.
- **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and the Game Design Document §4.4 shield
  entry.
- **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Visual only** — do not change the shield duration (15 s), absorb semantics
  (`tryAbsorbShield`), hit-gating, or any GDD §4.4 functional behaviour.
- A shield that **absorbs a hit** still pops immediately (no ending animation)
  — the pop path is unchanged.
- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (see `AGENTS.md` §Gym↔game parity): the
  ending animation must run in the gyms and the game from the same code.
- No new per-frame allocations or extra Graphics objects; the existing
  scene-owned bubble is redrawn in place each frame.
- Keep the existing exported constant values stable for the steady state so
  existing tests/consumers do not break.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` exports `drawShieldBubble(graphics,
  player, registry)` — the single shared drawing helper used by `PlayScene`
  (`_updateVisuals`), `GymPowerUpsCombat` (`_updateVisuals`) and
  `GymFormationScene` (`_updateVisuals`). It currently draws a fixed
  `lineStyle`/`fillStyle` circle at `SHIP_SIZE × SHIELD_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`
  (`1.6`) and clears when `!registry.isShielded`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` `EffectsRegistry` already exposes
  `remaining(id)` (seconds, `undefined` when inactive), `isShielded`, and
  `tick(dt)`; `P3_SHIELD_DURATION = 15`.
- The player hull radius is `SHIP_SIZE / 2` (10 px), so a fill radius below 10
  is visually smaller than the ship.
- `CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` already pins the steady-state constants and
  fake-Graphics call shapes, giving a ready test seam.

## Desired change

Extend the **single** shared helper `drawShieldBubble` so that, in addition to
the steady state, it reads `registry.remaining('P3')` and applies a
time-based ending animation in the last 1.0 s:

1. `remaining > 1.0 s` → current steady-state bubble (unchanged).
2. `0.5 s < remaining ≤ 1.0 s` → opaque fill ramps up; rim stroke alpha pulses.
3. `0 < remaining ≤ 0.5 s` → rim keeps pulsing; fill radius interpolates from
   `SHIP_SIZE × 1.6` down below `SHIP_SIZE / 2`.
4. `remaining ≤ 0` (shield expired/popped) → `graphics.clear()`, draw nothing,
   return `false`.

The animation must be a pure function of `remaining` (frame-rate independent),
so tests can drive it deterministically. New exported constants
(`SHIELD_BUBBLE_ENDING_SECONDS = 1.0`, `SHIELD_BUBBLE_SHRINK_SECONDS = 0.5`,
`SHIELD_BUBBLE_ENDING_FILL_ALPHA`, `SHIELD_BUBBLE_SHRINK_MIN_FACTOR`, pulse
rate) document the tuning surface.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — add the ending-animation
  constants and the time-based fill/rim/radius logic to `drawShieldBubble`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` — new unit tests for the four
  timeline phases and determinism.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — no behavioural change expected (consumer of the
  shared helper); comment may reference the animation.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — no behavioural change expected
  (consumer of the shared helper).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — no behavioural change expected
  (consumer of the shared helper).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 P3 shield row / implementation note
  describing the ending indicator.
- `README.md` — only if it describes shield visuals.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8QV3O9008JVNQ** — PlayScene: add P3 shield bubble visual + post-absorb
  blink (completed). Introduced the bubble + `tryAbsorbShield` pop; this item
  refines the *expiry* visual, not the pop.
- **AH-0MUICQC34005QOYF** — Add shield bubble and phase ghost to
  GymFormationScene (completed). Established the shared
  `CombatEffectVisuals` helper and gym parity this item builds on.
- **AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5** — PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual
  (completed). Sibling effect visual sharing the same helper.
- **AH-0MUICQCQM002WAAJ** — Document shared shield/phase gating (completed).
- **AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M** — Restore gym-game parity: wire missing power-up
  behaviours into PlayScene (RCA) (completed) — parent of the bubble work.

## Risks, assumptions & mitigations

- **Risk (scope creep):** adding new visual behaviour invites re-tuning of the
  steady-state bubble. *Mitigation:* keep steady-state constants frozen; tune
  only new ending constants. Extra ideas (e.g. audio cue) are linked as new
  work items, not folded in.
- **Risk (reads as functional change):** players may assume the shrinking fill
  means the shield no longer absorbs. *Mitigation:* the shield keeps absorbing
  until true expiry/pop; ACs pin functional semantics unchanged and docs note
  the animation is cosmetic only.
- **Risk (gym divergence):** a per-scene copy could drift. *Mitigation:* AC4
  forces all three scenes through the shared helper; the repository's
  duplicate-body guard and gym-parity tests enforce it.
- **Assumption:** "opaque" means a visibly solid-ish fill (alpha ramps to a
  documented high value such as ~0.6), not literally alpha `1.0` (which would
  hide the ship). Overridable by the producer.
- **Assumption:** the pulse keeps the existing shield blue (`0x3399ff`) with
  oscillating stroke alpha rather than switching to a warning colour (e.g.
  red), because the item does not request a colour change. Overridable.
- **Assumption:** the ending window starts at `T-1s` before natural expiry (per
  "for 1 second before fully disappearing"), not at the moment of expiry.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

These questions were previously raised on the work item (comment
`AH-C0MUD5X2DA00027Y0`, author Map) and had no producer answer at intake time.
Resolutions below are documented working assumptions used to complete the
brief; they remain open for producer override.

- **Q1: When should the pulse/fade start — at T-1s or at T=0?** — Working
  answer: **T-1s** (during the final second before natural expiry). Basis: the
  original text says "pulse the rim for 1 second **before** fully
  disappearing". Status: assumption, overridable.
- **Q2: What does "make the inside opaque" mean?** — Working answer: ramp the
  **fill alpha up** to a visibly opaque value (documented constant, e.g.
  ~0.6) at the start of the ending window, then shrink the shading. It is not
  a fade-to-nothing. Status: OPEN QUESTION — assumption applied for drafting,
  overridable.
- **Q3: Should the gyms (GymPowerUpsCombat / GymFormationScene) get the same
  animation?** — Working answer: **yes, automatically**, because all three
  scenes already draw through the one shared `drawShieldBubble` helper; the
  change lands there once. Basis: `AGENTS.md` gym↔game parity. Status:
  assumption aligned to repo convention.
- **Q4: Pulse colour — keep blue or use a warning colour?** — Working answer:
  keep the existing shield blue (`0x3399ff`) with oscillating stroke alpha.
  Status: assumption, overridable.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUH5I6EG002N5L5** – Re-base GymPowerUpsCombat on CombatScene (completed)
- **AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24** – Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle, collection, magnet, P4 notice, cues) (completed)
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** – Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the mineral kill-drop code with the game (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorb, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+282 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorb, absorbing, absorbs, ac1, ac2 (+278 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0x3399ff, absorb, absorbs, ac1, ac4 (+263 more)
data.title: Shields need to pulse and fade when ending

## Summary

Test that `_timeoutWave()` in `PlayScene.ts` keeps surviving non-asteroid enemies alive, removes the life penalty, resets the wave timer, and that survivors are fully active during the transition pause.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On timeout, surviving non-asteroid enemies remain alive at their current position.
2. The player does not lose a life on timeout.
3. The wave timer resets for the next wave.
4. Survivors move and fire during the 3s transition pause.
5. Survivors persist across level boundaries.
6. Survivors persist into the boss fight (asteroids cleared at boss entry per existing behaviour, but non-asteroid survivors remain).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

- Will test after Feature 6 is implemented.
- Use existing `bootPlayWithAsteroid` / `bootPlay` harnesses.
- Assert: `scene.getAliveCount()` unchanged by timeout, `lives` unchanged, `waveTimer` reset after transition.

## Summary

Replace `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` to keep survivors alive, remove life penalty, register survivors with WaveManager for gating, and advance wave/level.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Surviving non-asteroid enemies persist when timer expires — no detonation.
2. Player retains all lives on timeout.
3. Wave manager registers survivors for gating the next wave.
4. Wave/level advances normally after timeout.
5. Wave timer resets for the next wave.
6. Survivors are fully active during the 3s transition pause (move and attack).
7. Survivors persist across level boundaries.
8. Survivors persist into the boss fight (asteroids cleared at boss entry per existing behaviour).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()`, `_advanceAfterTimeout()`, transition handling
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `adoptCarriedSurvivors()` seam

## Implementation Notes

- Rewrite `_timeoutWave()`: filter survivors (exclude asteroids), register with WaveManager via `adoptCarriedSurvivors(count)`, advance wave/level via `_advanceAfterTimeout()`.
- Remove `detonateWaveTimeoutSurvivors()` call and `_loseLife(false)` call.
- Add `_moveCarriedSurvivors(dt)` during transition (call in `update()` alongside existing asteroid move).
- Add `_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions()` during transition (or reuse existing collision logic).
- Ensure survivors remain in `this.spawned` — they persist through the transition automatically.
- In `_onTransitionComplete`, do NOT clear survivors (existing code only clears asteroids for boss entry).

# Tests: dynamic opening variety, determinism and regression

**Parent:** AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B (Create more variety in the first 3-4 waves)

## Context

Test-first slice for the dynamic opening change. Add the acceptance tests for
the parent's AC1–AC6 before the implementation child makes them pass. The
parameters (pool, count floor, jitter, targets) come from the spike child.

## Scope

- Extend the regression describe block in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`
  with opening-wave assertions.
- Extend `src/core/configStore.test.ts` (default curve mode/target agreement).
- Extend `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` (CSV mode/target agreement).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 have `generation === 'dynamic'` and
  that every wave in levels 1–3 has `shootEnabled === false`, on
  `buildSequencedLevels()` output.
- A test asserts that at the default seed the four opening waves use at least
  three distinct archetypes and no two of the four share an identical
  composition.
- A test asserts at least two distinct seeds produce different opening
  compositions, and that each seed reproduces its campaign exactly (same-seed
  equality).
- A test asserts that across a seed sweep no opening wave (levels 1–3) is
  asteroid-only and none has a total count of 1.
- The existing AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins still pass unchanged: non-decreasing
  targets within and across levels, strictly rising aggregated difficulty, the
  fire boundary, and the levels 4–5 composition pins.
- A test asserts `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and
  `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` both mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` with matching
  targets, and that every other wave's mode and target is unchanged.
- Every new test fails before the implementation child and passes after it
  (red→green), and the full test suite passes after the implementation child.

- **Parent AC1 — Dynamic, non-firing opening** (covered): asserts the first four campaign waves (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2) have `generation: dynamic` and remain non-firing (`shootEnabled === false`), and the fire boundary for levels 1–3 is unchanged.
- **Parent AC2 — Real variety** (covered): asserts at least three distinct existing enemy archetypes appear across the four waves at the default seed and no two of the four waves share an identical composition.
- **Parent AC3 — Per-run variation with reproducibility** (covered): builds with at least two distinct run seeds and asserts variation plus same-seed campaign equality; curve/fixed waves stay seed-independent.
- **Parent AC4 — No regression of the retuned campaign** (covered): asserts no asteroid-only wave and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3, and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins (non-decreasing targets within and across levels, strictly rising aggregated difficulty, fire boundary held).
- **Parent AC5 — Defaults and seed agree** (covered): asserts `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` both mark L1W1..L2W2 dynamic with matching retuned targets, and every other wave's mode and target is unchanged.
- **Parent AC6 — Testing/validation** (covered): new unit/integration tests cover mode dispatch, seed variation and reproducibility, the non-degeneracy guarantee and the difficulty ramp; the full project test suite passes.

## Deliverables

- Committed test code encoding the parent AC1–AC6.
- A short note in the work item recording the red (pre-implementation) run.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the spike child (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B child 1) for the parameter
  values used in the seed-sweep assertions.

## Notes

- Test only observable public output (`buildSequencedLevels`,
  `defaultDifficultyCurves`, the CSV codec) — no private internals.
- UK English in test names and comments.
data.title: Tests: dynamic opening variety, determinism and regression

## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC1 — the Central AI spawns after Level 5 is cleared, with Phase-1 minions
- Failing commit: f4353700a0cd0e9dfad57f4e379d42ac3ca7e55b
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Full-suite run at HEAD f4353700a0cd0e9dfad57f4e379d42ac3ca7e55b: 3 failed | 2680 passed (2683) in src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts (boss encounter AC1/AC4 and AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC4). The same file passes in isolation (143/143), and the suite was green at the earlier HEAD e26b62fe, so this is a test-isolation/ordering regression surfacing after commits 8e7591d7/f4353700 (AH-0MUPP1Q7S009NFHE weapon-reset). Observed failure counts vary between runs (2-3), indicating non-determinism.
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout f4353700a0cd0e9dfad57f4e379d42ac3ca7e55b`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC1 — the Central AI spawns after Level 5 is cleared, with Phase-1 minions'` (or equivalent command)

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

# Per-weapon level state on Player

## Summary
Add per-weapon level tracking to the Player entity: a Map<WeaponId, number> for run-scoped levels, level-up logic on equipWeapon (temporary) and on mineral choice (permanent), level-persistence across weapon timeout, and level-resolved getWeaponDef returning the leveled WeaponDefinition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Player tracks a Map<WeaponId, number> for per-weapon run-scoped levels.
- AC2: Collecting a temporary weapon drop (equipWeapon) increments the weapon level and re-activates its timed duration.
- AC3: The level persists for the run even when the weapon times out (weapon stops firing but level is retained; re-collecting re-activates it at the same level).
- AC4: getWeaponDef(id) returns a level-resolved WeaponDefinition (or WeaponLevelStats) incorporating the current level.
- AC5: getWeaponLevel(id) returns the current level for a weapon (defaulting to 0 or 1 for uncollected weapons).
- AC6: resetWeapon() clears timed activations but retains levels (per intake assumption; pending producer confirmation of Reset-drop semantics -- see parent AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J open question).
- AC7: Reset/restart clears all levels (run-scoped).
- AC8: Existing weapon behaviour at level 0/1 is unchanged (no regression).

## Key Files
- src/entities/Player.ts -- _weaponLevels Map, level-up on equipWeapon, level-resolved getWeaponDef, getWeaponLevel
- src/utils/weapons.ts -- extend WeaponDefinition or create WeaponLevelStats interface

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver provides resolveWeaponAtLevel

## Deliverables
- Player.ts with _weaponLevels, getWeaponLevel, level-resolved getWeaponDef
- Updated equipWeapon, resetWeapon, resetWeaponTimers
- Back-compat: level 0/1 behaves identically to current unlevelled behaviour
data.title: Feature: Per-weapon level state on Player

# Apply leveled effects in shared combat core (>=4 variables)

## Summary
Wire the level-resolved weapon definition into the shared auto-fire path (CombatCoreScene._autoFire) so that >=4 upgrade variables measurably change weapon behaviour at higher levels. Same code path for game (PlayScene) and gyms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: CombatCoreScene._autoFire consumes the level-resolved weapon definition (via player.getWeaponDef) for bullet pattern/colour/size/lifetime/speed.
- AC2: The four producer-confirmed MVP upgrade variables measurably change weapon behaviour at higher levels: fire rate, projectile count, bullet size, and AoE radius (confirmed 2026-10-02).
- AC3: The same level-resolution code path is used by PlayScene and all gyms that exercise weapons (no divergent copies).
- AC4: New variables (e.g. piercing, AoE) are applied through the shared combat core, not scene-specific code.
- AC5: The duplicate-body/equivalence guard in CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts continues to pass (gym-game parity verified).

## Key Files
- src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts -- consume level-resolved def in _autoFire, apply piercing/damage/AoE
- src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts -- shared bullet spawning respects new variables
- src/scenes/gym/ -- update gym weapon exercises to use leveled weapons

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver, variable catalogue, Player level state

## Deliverables
- CombatCoreScene.ts with level-resolved bullet spawning
- CombatScene.ts shared path supporting new variables
- Updated gym weapon exercises

# Fire-rate upgrade quantised to beat grid

## Summary
Ensure that fire-rate upgrades from weapon leveling never produce off-grid intervals. Level-resolved fire rates are quantised to valid beat subdivisions, preserving AC6 (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The level resolver maps fire-rate upgrades to valid beat subdivisions (e.g. 2/beat, 3/beat, 4/beat, 6/beat) -- no arbitrary intervals.
- AC2: The catalogue-wide isOnBeatGrid invariant holds for every weapon at every level (1..100).
- AC3: Property tests verify isOnBeatGrid for all weapons at levels 1..100.
- AC4: If the next subdivision would be off-grid, the system falls back to the nearest valid subdivision.
- AC5: The beat grid test (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ precedent) passes with leveled weapons.

## Key Files
- src/utils/weaponLevels.ts -- fire-rate quantisation in resolveWeaponAtLevel
- src/utils/weapons.ts -- isOnBeatGrid validation at level resolution
- src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts -- property test: isOnBeatGrid at all levels

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver (fire-rate curve + quantisation)

## Deliverables
- Fire-rate quantisation logic in weaponLevels.ts
- isOnBeatGrid property test at all levels
- Updated isOnBeatGrid invariant check in weapons.ts if needed

# Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling

## Summary
Extend the mineral choice system so that when the player has active weapons, the mineral choice offers weapon level-up options alongside the existing power-up choices. Applying a weapon level-up permanently raises that weapon level.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The mineral choice offers weapon level-up options (leveling an existing weapon by 1) in the pool of available choices.
- AC2: The offered options reflect current weapon levels (higher-level weapons are more attractive offers).
- AC3: Applying a permanent weapon level-up calls Player.equipWeapon(id, true) and increments the weapon permanent level.
- AC4: The mineral choice pool (CHOICE_POOL) is extended with weapon-level-up entries that reference current player weapon levels.
- AC5: If the player has no weapons beyond the cannon, the choice pool falls back to existing behaviour (no weapon-level-up offers).
- AC6: The offer count remains 3 (producer-confirmed 2026-10-02: keep the existing 3-offer mechanism).

## Key Files
- src/powerups/choice.ts -- extend CHOICE_POOL with weapon level-up entries, pluggable strategy
- src/powerups/types.ts -- new choice type for weapon level-up
- src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts -- apply permanent weapon level-up via Player.equipWeapon(id, true)

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver, Player level state, pluggable power-up choice strategy (related work AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX)

## Deliverables
- Extended CHOICE_POOL with weapon level-up options
- New weapon level-up choice type
- mineralLayer.ts to apply permanent level-up
data.title: Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling

# HUD weapon level readout

## Summary
Display each active weapon level in the HUD so the player can see their weapon progression. One row per active weapon showing weapon name, level, and optionally a visual indicator (e.g. level dots or bar).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The HUD displays each active weapon with its current level (e.g. Cannon Lv.3, Spread Lv.2).
- AC2: The level is read from the player level map via player.getWeaponLevel(id).
- AC3: When a weapon levels up, the HUD updates to reflect the new level (reactive update).
- AC4: Weapons at level 0/1 display without a level suffix or with Lv.1 (design decision).
